claims.statement: OpenHands is a community-driven platform for developing AI agents that interact with the world through software interfaces (code execution, command line, web browsing).
confidence_reasons: Multiple design choices support this claim
claims.quote: OpenHands, a platform for the development of powerful and flexible AI agents that interact with the world in similar ways to those of a human developer

claims.statement: CodeActAgent v1.8 with claude-3.5-sonnet achieves competitive performance on SWE-Bench Lite, reaching 26.0% resolve rate on 300 instances without hint text.
claims.quote: CodeActAgent v1.8, using claude-3.5-sonnet, achieves a competitive resolve rate of 26%

claims.statement: Model selection significantly impacts performance, with claude-3.5-sonnet (26.0%) substantially outperforming gpt-4o-mini (6.3%) on SWE-Bench Lite.
confidence_reasons: Controlled conditions differ only by model

claims.statement: CodeActAgent v1.5 achieves 79.3% pass rate on HumanEvalFix Python subset using 0-shot multi-turn evaluation with self-debugging.
claims.quote: OpenHands CodeActAgent successfully fixes 79.3% of bugs in the Python split

claims.statement: CodeActAgent 0-shot approach on HumanEvalFix is significantly better than non-agentic baselines and almost doubles StarCoder2-15B performance.
confidence_reasons: Comparison details not fully specified in evidence
claims.quote: significantly better than all non-agentic approaches, almost doubling the performance of StarCoder2-15B

claims.statement: OpenHands achieves competitive performance across diverse task categories (software engineering, web browsing, miscellaneous) using the same CodeAct agent without prompt modifications.
confidence_reasons: Multiple evidence points from different benchmarks
claims.quote: the same CodeAct agent, without any modifications to its system prompt, demonstrates competitive performance across three major task categories

claims.statement: WebArena: BrowsingAgent v1.0 achieves 8.5-15.5% on 812 WebArena instances using domain-general zero-shot prompting.
CodeActAgent v1.5 achieves 52.0% accuracy on GPQA diamond set (198 graduate-level questions), compared to expert human performance of 81.3%.
MINT math: CodeActAgent v1.5 with gpt-4o achieves 77.3% on math tasks with up to 5 iterations of agent-tool-human feedback.
ProofWriter: CodeActAgent v1.5 achieves 78.8% on the challenging 5-hop deductive reasoning subset (600 instances).
OpenHands supports 15 established benchmarks spanning software engineering (7), web browsing (2), and miscellaneous assistance (6) domains.
claims.quote: we integrate 15 established benchmarks into OpenHands

claims.statement: OpenHands has received 32K GitHub stars and 2.1K+ contributions from 188+ contributors as a community-driven open-source project.
claims.quote: OpenHands has gained significant traction, with 32K GitHub stars and more than 2.1K contributions from over 188 contributors

claims.statement: Current agents struggle with complex tasks and file editing performance, particularly on long files.
claims.quote: Current agents still struggle with complex tasks, and we are interested in exploring different approaches to improve the file editing performance of agents

claims.statement: OpenHands workflow currently requires substantial handcrafted workload for agent construction.
claims.quote: OpenHands's workflow still requires a substantial handcrafted workload

claims.statement: OpenHands enables systematic evaluation to identify and address agent risks before widespread deployment.
confidence_reasons: Stated as goal/hypothesis rather than demonstrated result
claims.quote: OpenHands helps mitigate risks by: (1) Enabling systematic evaluation of these agents, which can identify and address risks before they are widely deployed

claims.statement: MiniWoB++ full set evaluation (125 environments) requires handling tasks that need vision capability.
claims.quote: it contains a portion of environments that require vision capability to tackle successfully

claims.statement: BIRD benchmark was extended to enable multi-turn interactions for agents to correct historical SQL results via execution feedback.
claims.quote: we extend the setting by allowing the agent to engage in multi-turn interactions to arrive at the final SQL query

claims.statement: OpenHands Docker runtime uses dual-tagging system (hash-based for reproducibility, generic for latest version) to balance reproducibility and flexibility.
claims.quote: OpenHands uses a dual-tagging system for its runtime images to balance reproducibility with flexibility

claims.statement: OpenHands integration test framework uses LLM mocking with exact prompt matches to enable deterministic testing while reducing evaluation costs.
confidence_reasons: Explicit technical description of testing approach
claims.quote: the framework intercepts all LLM calls and supplies predefined responses based on exact prompt matches

limitations.statement: Agent performance varies significantly by model choice (4x difference between claude-3.5-sonnet and gpt-4o-mini on SWE-Bench).
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Claims about 'competitive performance' must specify model used; generalizability across models is limited

limitations.statement: Many evaluation results use small benchmark subsets for cost reasons (e.g., SWE-Bench Lite vs full SWE-Bench).
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Results may not generalize to full benchmarks; cost-driven evaluation choices affect scope

limitations.statement: Current OpenHands agents struggle with complex tasks and file editing, particularly on long files.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Practical applicability limited for complex real-world software engineering tasks

limitations.statement: OpenHands workflow construction requires substantial handcrafted workload.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Automation claims are limited; manual engineering overhead remains significant

limitations.statement: HumanEvalFix benchmark allows theoretical 100% performance, making 79.3% not a fundamental limit.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Room for improvement exists; not reaching ceiling performance indicates capability gaps

limitations.statement: MiniWoB++ evaluation on full set (125 environments) includes tasks requiring vision capability where agents may not be optimized.
limitations.effect_on_interpretation: Performance includes vision-dependent tasks where multimodal limitations apply

negative_result_decisions.reason: Demonstrates model sensitivity and guides selection for practitioners; important for reproducibility
